title: Warring States Japan
capsule: The Sengoku period (戦国時代, 'Warring States era') was a century of near-continuous civil war in Japan, conventionally dated from the Ōnin War (1467–1477) that devastated Kyoto and paralysed the Ashikaga shogunate, leaving provincial daimyo to contest territorial control. Regional strongmen such as Oda Nobunaga, who began his conquests in Owari in the 1550s, gradually consolidated power through musket-equipped armies and castle-town economies; Nobunaga's assassination in 1582 was followed by the rise of Toyotomi Hideyoshi, who completed national unification by 1590. The period's formal end is placed at the Battle of Sekigahara (1600) or the siege of Osaka Castle (1615), after which Tokugawa Ieyasu's shogunate imposed a durable peace.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Daimyo domains in the Sengoku period shifted frequently and are incompletely recorded; territorial reconstructions rely on later cadastral surveys and vary significantly among historians.
